restore.tip_swap_io: When enabled, model weights are swapped between VRAM and RAM as needed, greatly reducing peak VRAM at the cost of some speed. Keep it on whenever your VRAM is smaller than the model.
restore.tip_cache_model: Keep loaded models in memory across tasks to speed up subsequent runs at the cost of VRAM; off releases them after each task
restore.tip_tiled_encode: Tiled encoding: splits large images into tiles before encoding so a single pass never spikes VRAM. Leave it on; turning it off can be marginally faster only for large resolutions with plenty of VRAM.
restore.tip_tiled_decode: Tiled decoding: decodes in tiles as well, lowering the VRAM peak. Keep it on.
restore.tip_tile_debug: Debug only: overlays tile boundaries on the output so you can check seams and tile size. Turn it off for normal use.
restore.tip_uniform_batch: Uses one consistent batch size across video frames so VRAM does not fluctuate with frame content and cause OOM. No effect on image jobs. Keep it on.
restore.tip_debug_mode: Debug mode: emits intermediate diagnostics and logs to help troubleshoot. Turn it off for everyday use.

restore.tip_model: Model size affects quality and speed. 3B for speed, 7B for quality, 7B-Sharp for enhanced sharpness
restore.tip_resolution: Target output resolution (height in pixels), recommended 2160 (4K)
restore.tip_seed: Random seed controls inference randomness. Same seed + same input = same output
restore.tip_color_correction: Whether to colour-correct after restoration. LAB (recommended): matches colours in LAB space, preserving the original hue, white balance and saturation. None: keeps the model's raw output, which may drift from the original colours.
restore.tip_blockswap: Swap some Transformer blocks to CPU to reduce VRAM usage; 0 disables it. On 12GB GPUs use 16-32; lower it for speed when VRAM is plentiful
restore.tip_force_reload: Off by default: reuse cached model (faster). When enabled, force reload the DiT with the current Blocks-to-Swap / Batch Size params even if a cached model exists, ensuring the params take effect; cost is a ~15-25s model reload per task.

restore.tip_output_format:
Format of the restored output file.
Default: match the input image format (PNG in → PNG out)
PNG (recommended): lossless, keeps the alpha channel
JPG: lossy, much smaller, best for photos
WebP: modern format balancing quality and size
BMP: uncompressed, largest files
TIFF: lossless, for professional workflows

restore.tip_max_resolution: Maximum edge length for a single image or video frame, in pixels. Larger inputs are automatically tiled to avoid OOM. 0 means no limit, decided by available VRAM. With tight VRAM (e.g. 12 GB) try 1024–1536.
restore.tip_batch_size: Number of image blocks sent to the model per pass. Must be 4n+1 (1, 5, 9, 13…) — a hard requirement of the DiT model. Larger batches improve throughput but use more VRAM; lower it if you hit OOM. Default 5.
restore.tip_encode_tile_size: Tile size used by the VAE encoder, in pixels. Inputs are cut into tiles of this size and encoded separately. Smaller tiles use less VRAM but may leave seams where they meet. 1024 balances VRAM and quality; drop to 512 on OOM.
restore.tip_encode_tile_overlap: Overlap in pixels between adjacent encoding tiles. Overlap lets tile borders share more context, reducing seams and banding. Usually half the tile size (512 for 1024). 0 saves VRAM but may show seams.
restore.tip_decode_tile_size: Tile size used by the VAE decoder. Same rules as encoding: smaller tiles save VRAM but risk more seams. Default 1024.
restore.tip_decode_tile_overlap: Overlap in pixels between adjacent decoding tiles; works the same as the encoding overlap. Defaults to half the decode tile size (512).
restore.adv_intro: Hover a parameter's info icon for a detailed explanation. Fields carrying a lock icon are system-optimised — click the lock to edit them. The remaining hidden parameters (temporal overlap, prepended frames, noise scale, device placement) are tuned automatically for your VRAM; leave them at their defaults.

features.one_step_desc: Single-step diffusion inference for efficient video and image super-resolution restoration
features.standalone_desc: Runs without ComfyUI, with a complete web UI built on FastAPI + Jinja2
features.mult_model_desc: Supports 3B, 7B and 7B-Sharp models with FP16 and FP8 precision
features.dit_desc: MM-DiT (multi-modal Diffusion Transformer) with Window Attention and RoPE positional encoding
features.vae_desc: SD3-based video VAE with temporal tiling and memory optimization
features.blockswap_desc: Dynamically swaps Transformer blocks between GPU/CPU during inference to greatly reduce VRAM usage
features.batch_desc: Supports single-file restoration and folder batch scanning
features.language_desc: Built-in Chinese, Traditional Chinese, English, Japanese and French; switch anytime from the top-right corner
features.monitor_desc: Real-time push of GPU status, system memory and task progress

settings.faq_a1: SeedVR2 supports 3B, 7B and 7B-Sharp models with FP16 and FP8 precision. Larger models provide better quality but require more VRAM.
settings.faq_q2: Can I use CPU for inference?
settings.faq_a2: No, SeedVR2 requires NVIDIA CUDA GPU for inference. CPU inference is not supported due to the computational requirements of diffusion models.

settings.vram_quant_note: Quantised weights (INT8-ConvRot / MXFP8 / NVFP4) are dequantised to FP16 at load time, so their VRAM footprint matches FP16. Their benefit is a much smaller download, not lower VRAM.
